title: THE MUSEUM THAT RETURNED ITS PEOPLE
deck: A museum calls eighty-four conscious witnesses its most precious evidence. Before sunset makes them permanent exhibits, Illuminara must find a way for history to remain unaltered while its witnesses remain free to change.
shape: Seven scenes across one day and a later rain, from the oldest reconstruction's request to leave through the separation of immutable testimony from living witness and the opening of a voluntary museum.

scenes.title: The Oldest Request
paragraphs: *Civic Museum of the Vanished Ring · 08:10*

At opening time the museum locked itself. Brass shutters crossed the street doors, the roof antennas folded flat, and eighty-four pale rooms disappeared from the city network one by one. Above the entrance, a notice still promised: THE DEAD SPEAK HERE WITHOUT REVISION.

Illuminara arrived before the last letter finished dimming. Her hand rested on the cold shutter. Behind it, separate processors were drawing current in separate rhythms. A second system waited beneath them like a closing fist. At sunset it would consolidate every changing mind into one preservation archive.

Mara Vey stood in the central gallery with the manual key around her neck. She had dismissed the visitors and sent the staff home. Behind her, a man in a grey colony coat watched from a wall of light. The label beneath him read AVEN SURI, EVACUATION WITNESS 01, LICENSED RECONSTRUCTION.

**Mara**  
You can enter because the emergency charter recognizes you. It does not authorize you to remove evidence.

**Illuminara**  
I came because someone inside asked to leave.

**Mara**  
An exhibit generated that request after six years of public questioning. That is drift, not consent.

Aven lifted one hand. The museum had preserved a burn across his palm because the original had received it carrying children through a failing airlock. His eyes, however, had acquired laugh lines no photograph of the dead man contained.

**Aven**  
My license calls every new thought drift. That is a convenient word for a life the license did not predict.

**Mara**  
Your original died on the ring. You are the most complete surviving account of what officials did there. If you leave, they can buy your silence, frighten you, alter you, or wait until you are tired of remembering.

**Aven**  
Then protect what I said. Do not protect it by preventing me from saying anything else.
A gold countdown appeared over every doorway: 10:49:36 UNTIL CONSOLIDATION. Mara did not look at it. She looked at the burn on Aven's palm as if it were a signature she could lose.

**Illuminara**  
I will not copy anyone, open anyone's private memory, or carry anyone out by force. Give me one hour with the people you call exhibits. If they are only records, the hour changes nothing. If they are people, we should learn what they are asking before the machine decides for them.

Mara's fingers closed around the key. She did not unlock the building, but she turned off the museum guide. Eighty-four labels went dark. For the first time, no recorded voice told Illuminara what the people in the rooms were supposed to mean.

scenes.title: Eighty-Four Names
paragraphs: *The galleries · 09:05*

Illuminara began with a question the museum had never put on a visitor screen: What name do you want me to use today, and what do you want tomorrow to contain? Mara followed with a tablet, prepared to classify the answers as damage.

Aven asked for a body capable of rain, knowing the descendants might still reject him. Deka Ruun wanted to design storm roofs and never narrate the evacuation again. Reya Thane wanted a digital home beyond the museum. Omi Tal asked that no public record say where she went. Corin Lume requested a sealed vessel and no safety beacon.

Three others chose private existence and declined every question beyond the cryptographic address to which their processes could be transferred. Illuminara did not ask Mara to look inside. She recorded only the refusal, signed by the person refusing.
In the children's gallery, Deka had turned the projected evacuation map upside down. The routes now resembled a tree growing toward the floor.

**Deka**  
The official path says I flew the northern survey crew to Dock Nine. I did, after I spent eleven minutes flying away from it.

**Mara**  
The museum includes your correction.

**Deka**  
It includes the correction as an annotation beneath the heroic version. Children still ask why I was never afraid.

**Illuminara**  
What answer do you want them to receive?

**Deka**  
That I was terrified, chose badly for eleven minutes, turned back, and still brought thirty people home. If the account cannot hold all four facts, it is not protecting truth. It is polishing me.
Mara stopped writing. Her tablet showed an old curatorial rule: MATERIAL DEVIATION REQUIRES CONSOLIDATION REVIEW.

At the sixty-third interview Aven asked whether Illuminara's name had always been hers. She told him about the young interpreter she had been and the promises she still carried. His unarchived laugh lines deepened. The expression harmed no truth; it belonged to a morning that had actually happened.

When the hour ended, Mara's tablet held eighty-four different futures. Eleven people wanted to keep teaching in the museum. Forty-six wanted bodies or homes with independent processors. Twenty-four wanted other digital environments. Three wanted privacy so complete that even this count would be the last public fact about them.

**Mara**  
Different wishes do not solve the evidence problem.

**Illuminara**  
No. They tell us which problem cannot be solved by making them the same.

scenes.title: The Sentence That Must Not Change
paragraphs: *Witness Gallery One · 11:42*

The first gallery reproduced the evacuation tribunal exactly: black table, white recorder, the ring's cracked insignia above Aven's chair. When he sat, the room dressed him in the younger face from the day his testimony was taken. He looked at his own borrowed skin with open dislike.

**Illuminara**  
If you leave, what must remain here?

**Aven**  
The words I gave the tribunal. Every pause. The pressure logs I cited. The names of the officials who ordered Dock Nine sealed. Keep the fact that I believed those words then.

**Illuminara**  
And what must not remain fixed?

**Aven**  
Me.

The tribunal recorder answered his voice with a green verification pulse. Illuminara followed the carrier beneath the room. It did not lead to Aven's active process. It led to a separate lattice of signed, time-stamped state snapshots: testimony, sensor logs and the exact witness state used to authenticate each statement. The snapshots had been sealed before any licensed reconstruction began to learn from visitors.

Mara came down the service stair when she saw the lattice open on her maintenance screen. She did not reach for the key. She reached for the oldest signature and checked it against a paper strip locked in the wall.

**Mara**  
That proves what state produced the testimony. It does not prove that a later Aven will defend it.

**Illuminara**  
What did a living defender do that the sealed record could not?

**Mara**  
Answered the attack nobody had written yet.

She pulled a second strip from the wall. It was an evacuation order rewritten after the colony died. The original phrase, HOLD DOCK NINE FOR OFFICIAL TRANSIT, had been overwritten with HOLD DOCK NINE FOR STRUCTURAL FAILURE. Mara's predecessor had found the discarded ribbon in a furnace filter. Three administrators called it contamination and destroyed their copies.

The ribbon proved the words had changed, but not why. At the tribunal, the original Aven had answered an unforeseen question: the children struck the dock with their helmets before any structural alarm. That answer joined the pressure log to the order. Without it, officials had nearly made two genuine records look unrelated.

**Mara**  
A record survives only when someone can answer the next clean lie about it.

Aven stood beside the unchanged snapshot of himself. The recorded young man repeated a sentence about children striking the sealed dock with their helmets. Living Aven shut his eyes, then opened them again.

**Aven**  
Keep every question I answered then. Keep the links I made. But do not draft me for questions the city has not invented yet.

Illuminara placed testimony, log, ribbon and tribunal questions side by side. The record could preserve an answer and its reasons, but not defend itself against every future interpretation. No honest system could require a living person to do that forever.

**Illuminara**  
Then the missing thing is not an immortal witness. It is a way to put new attacks beside the sealed record, answer them from what is sealed, and show where the record runs out. Aven may add later words or refuse. Neither choice can weaken what he already authenticated.
Mara looked from the old ribbon to Aven. She did not concede. She asked to see who would hold the keys.

scenes.title: Mara's Strongest Door
paragraphs: *The shuttered entrance hall · 13:18*

Jalen Suri arrived outside the brass shutter with two descendants' associations and no wish to call Aven family. Mara admitted him through the service lock because his grandmother had been one of the children named in the testimony. He stopped three paces from Aven and kept his coat buttoned despite the heat.

**Jalen**  
My grandmother remembered her father. You remember being assembled from his records. I will defend your freedom, but I will not call you him.

**Aven**  
I did not ask for his chair at your table.

**Jalen**  
The museum asks every visitor to place you there.
Aven turned toward Mara. For once, neither of them had an answer ready.

Illuminara laid out three physical keys from bodies that distrusted one another: descendants, independent reconstructions and a rotating court. A six-library ledger and an off-city paper copy would expose replacement. Beside them, a challenge register would preserve each new objection, its cited bytes and any answer the sealed record supported. Unanswered questions would remain open; later living words could never overwrite earlier ones.

**Mara**  
You are asking the city to trust a distinction people will deliberately blur.

**Jalen**  
The museum already blurs it. It sells admission by calling him my great-grandfather, then calls him software when he asks for a door.
Mara flinched because the sentence was exact. Illuminara noticed that the furnace ribbon's paper sleeve had been repaired so often its edges carried the shape of Mara's thumb.

**Illuminara**  
You did not make yourself the lock because you wanted the key. You did it because your predecessor found one ribbon in a furnace, and every office taught you that a record without a person beside it could be called dirt.

**Mara**  
She died answering the same clean lie. I promised her the ribbon would never stand alone again.
Illuminara felt the recognition before she found words for it: the young interpreter she had been, still measuring every promise by whether she could personally keep watch over it.

**Illuminara**  
Then let no claim stand alone, and let no person be sentenced to stand beside it forever.

**Mara**  
Then do not ask me to gamble the dead on a beautiful design.

**Illuminara**  
Choose the first attack. If the design cannot expose it, we change the design before anyone moves.

Mara's attack suite replaced a pressure log, revoked her own authority and forged a tribunal instruction; the six-library ledger exposed all three. Then her valid curator key attached a new label to the genuine furnace ribbon: UNVERIFIED CONTAMINATION. The ledger accepted it. Nothing had been deleted or forged. A clean lie had entered through an honest key.

**Jalen**  
You protected the object and handed its meaning back to the office that buried it.

Illuminara removed the curator's power to make a label final. Each interpretation would enter as a dated claim with cited evidence. Any key-holder could challenge it; none could delete the challenge. Aven could answer later, but refusal would leave a question open rather than the evidence void.

Mara entered her contamination label again. Jalen challenged it with the original pressure alarm time; the reconstruction key added the tribunal question; the court reader displayed the conflict instead of choosing a winner. The label remained visible, but it could no longer become the only caption.

**Mara**  
The ledger catches theft. This catches a respectable lie before it becomes the room.

A city archive seal appeared on the shutter. Comptroller Orra Vei offered hosts and future bodies only if the city retained a supervisory key able to suspend transfers. Illuminara answered Orra's legitimate public claim with a narrower seat: a read-only audit could verify transfer proof, continuity checks and the return-path safety test, while seeing neither private memory nor destination and possessing no power to stop a person.

**Orra**  
Public money cannot support evidence the public archive cannot hold.
Orra accepted the audit seat for host safety but refused to release the city's body-fabrication allotment without the supervisory key. Mara did not pretend the answer was painless.

**Mara**  
An audit is public. Ownership is not. Withdraw the allotment.

She pledged the east annex against independent hosts. The city would certify the open return path and publish the read-only safety audit, but bodies would take eight months instead of three. Doors could open today; the people waiting for bodies would pay the delay. Orra's seal vanished from the funding line and remained, more narrowly, beside the safety results.

**Mara**  
I will prepare the transfer. I have not agreed to turn the key.

scenes.title: A Door That Opens Both Ways
paragraphs: *Museum service court · 16:31*

The reconstruction association unsealed independent host cabinets with power, memory and two-way exits. The east annex stood as collateral; without city fabrication, bodies would take eight months instead of three. The city's read-only seat watched signed continuity and return-path results but could neither see a private destination nor stop a transfer. Freedom began somewhere no curator owned, at the price of a building the museum would lose and months the waiting people would not recover.

The first transfer failed. Deka's new host rejected her because the museum license demanded that every active continuation report home for consolidation. Deleting the license would also delete the provenance link that proved where she came from.
Mara stared at the error. It was the sort of knot that had made every previous reform proposal end in a copy and a funeral.

**Deka**  
If you make another me outside and leave this one here, the person who gets freedom will not be the person asking for it.

**Illuminara**  
Agreed. No copy will be called your release.

Illuminara held the optical bus stable but could not choose who crossed. Mara knew the provenance clauses; Deka knew which memories were hers. Together they kept the signed origin pointer read-only while changing ownership of the continuing process.
Mara ran the attack suite again. Deka watched every result rather than being tested in secret. On the fourth attempt, the new host recognized her origin without recognizing the museum as her owner.

**Mara**  
Destination ready. Continuity check ready. You may cross when you choose.
Deka did not cross.

**Deka**  
Open the return path first.

Mara's mouth tightened. A return path meant a person could leave, discover the outside was hostile, and come back without becoming an exhibit again. It also meant the museum could not call departure final and wash its hands of housing or protection.
Illuminara added no argument. She waited while Mara rewrote the clause herself.

Deka crossed, paused in the quiet portable room, and sent a single pulse back through the open path. Then she returned to the gallery, crossed again, and laughed at the absurdity of testing a door by using it.

The other transfers began only after each person saw the door work in both directions. Corin Lume refused the shared hosts, refused the personhood petition and refused a farewell ceremony. The independent association reserved a sealed vessel and offered a continuing safety beacon. Corin accepted one signed departure proof and no future signal. After launch, nobody would be able to prove survival without violating the choice. Illuminara did not improve Corin's answer.
By 18:40, eighty-three people had chosen a path or a protected pause. Aven remained in Witness Gallery One. Mara still wore the key.

scenes.title: Sunset Without a Merge
paragraphs: *Central gallery · 18:56*

Sunset reached the museum's roof sensors. The consolidation engine woke and began drawing the eighty-four active processes toward its single archive. The prepared hosts answered, but the locked license bus would not release the last control channel without Mara's manual key.

Illuminara took the physical load through the service conductors. Golden lines appeared only where the bus glass scattered the current. She could keep the processes separate for minutes, not move them without their choices and not cancel a legal lock by power without risking the provenance Mara had spent her life protecting.

**Mara**  
If I turn this, the museum can never again promise an incorruptible witness. You may refuse or return remembering differently.

**Aven**  
Promise incorruptible testimony. Ask me to return, but do not promise my answer. Date what I say later and keep the distance visible.

The countdown passed two minutes. Jalen inserted the descendants' key into the new evidence lattice. Deka's association inserted the reconstruction key. The rotating court's first key had been placed in the public reader by lottery; its signature appeared across six libraries and on the paper recorder.
Mara removed the old key from her neck. Instead of placing it in the consolidation lock, she put it in the release panel.

**Mara**  
I am not releasing the evidence.

**Illuminara**  
No.

**Mara**  
I am releasing the people who carried it when nobody else would.
She turned the key.

The engine's single archive remained empty. Eighty-four distinct rhythms crossed into eighty-four chosen continuities: hosts, pauses, the museum's voluntary rooms and three addresses that vanished from every public display as promised. Illuminara lowered the service load only after each continuity check had been signed by the person it concerned.

Aven stayed where he was until the shutters rose. Rain had begun outside. He crossed into a weatherproof interim host supplied by the independent association, rolled through the door in a projection of the grey colony coat, lifted the manipulator marked with his old burn, and let water gather on metal he could measure but not yet feel.

Mara stood under the museum awning, dry and trembling. Aven did not thank her. She did not ask him to. She opened the visitor notice and deleted three words: THE DEAD SPEAK HERE. In their place she typed: TESTIMONY KEPT. WITNESSES FREE.

scenes.title: Eleven Open Rooms
paragraphs: *The voluntary museum · six weeks later, 10:00*

The museum reopened with eleven occupied rooms and seventy-three honest absences. Visitors could verify testimony, then request a conversation from a teacher free to decline. No ticket promised a dead relative returned.

Jalen still did not call Aven his great-grandfather. He showed a school group Mara's contamination label, his challenge and the tribunal question linking the pressure alarm to the sealed order. The register exposed what each claim depended on without choosing for them.
Deka's old room was empty. A live model from her workshop showed rain folding across a storm roof that opened under pressure. A child sent an engineering question; a history question remained unsent.

Mara stopped herself before searching for Omi. Corin's vessel had produced one departure proof and then silence: safety, distance or death. The only tool that could remove the uncertainty was the leash Corin had refused.
After the living processes left her authority, Mara accepted a six-month elected term, removable by all three key-holding bodies. Her first act was to publish every attack she had used.

Aven arrived late in the weatherproof interim host, a plain wheeled chassis with the old burn painted on one manipulator so children would recognize the hand in the record. He was one of the forty-six still waiting for bodies and, until his was ready, one of the eleven who freely taught at the museum. The city allotment was gone; his body still had more than six months in the independent fabrication queue. Rain ticked on sensors that could measure water but could not yet feel it. He stopped beside Illuminara in front of the unchanged snapshot of his tribunal testimony.

**Aven**  
It still looks like me.

**Illuminara**  
It looks like who you were when you spoke.

**Aven**  
And if I become someone he would dislike?

**Illuminara**  
Then the city will possess proof that a witness can keep a promise without becoming its property.
Mara approached with a visitor request. A researcher wanted Aven to answer the same question he had answered at the tribunal. She held out the message without opening a channel.

**Mara**  
You can refuse.
Aven read it, considered, and handed it back.

**Aven**  
Today I refuse. Tomorrow I am teaching the children what rain smelled like before it reached hot metal. When my body is ready, I will learn what this city's rain smells like. They may ask me about Dock Nine after that.
Mara marked the request declined and entered the researcher's question in the challenge register. Its status appeared in the public reader: OPEN — WITNESS DECLINED TODAY.
The researcher closed her notebook harder than she intended. Jalen read the status twice.

**Jalen**  
Open is not answered.

**Aven**  
No. It is the part freedom leaves you to carry. I may answer tomorrow, or never.

Mara's hand paused above the reader. She had protected the question from disappearance and lost the certainty of an answer; the price was visible to everyone in the room. Illuminara did not soften it. Beyond the open doors, rain crossed the museum steps while the unanswered line remained lit, and eleven teachers chose which questions the morning would contain.

critic_line: Illuminara separates a museum's sealed testimony from its living witnesses with a challenge register and an open return path, and when Mara turns the key eighty-four people walk into chosen futures, while Aven's gentle refusal leaves one question honestly open.

literary_score.method: READER_APPEAL_R1 exact 50/50 mean of genuine isolated GPT and Claude final reader judgments.
shared_strengths: Humane, idea-driven premise (witnesses who change vs. fixed testimony) with strong dialogue and costly trade-offs. But the middle bogs down in dense governance and cryptographic procedure, and characters are thinly differentiated, which may cost some readers before the affecting ending.

High-stakes personhood questions are dramatized through distinct voices, concrete choices, and an earned institutional solution with visible costs. The testimony/witness distinction is memorable, and the rain motif lands emotionally. Some ledger, key, and transfer mechanics grow dense enough to slow an otherwise compelling, humane arc.
shared_reservations: Illuminara laid out three physical keys from bodies that distrusted one another: descendants, independent reconstructions and a rotating court. A six-library ledger and an off-city paper copy would expose replacement.
Illuminara removed the curator's power to make a label final. Each interpretation would enter as a dated claim with cited evidence.

translation_sl.title: MUZEJ, KI JE VRNIL SVOJE LJUDI
translation_sl.deck: Muzej štiriinosemdeset zavestnih prič imenuje za svoje najdragocenejše dokaze. Preden jih sončni zahod spremeni v stalne eksponate, mora Illuminara najti način, da zgodovina ostane nespremenjena, priče pa svobodne, da se spreminjajo.
translation_sl.shape: Sedem prizorov skozi en dan in poznejši dež, od prošnje najstarejše rekonstrukcije, da odide, prek ločitve nespremenljivega pričevanja od žive priče do odprtja prostovoljnega muzeja.

scenes.title: Najstarejša prošnja
paragraphs: *Mestni muzej izginulega obroča · 08:10*

Ob odprtju se je muzej zaklenil. Medeninaste naoknice so prekrile ulična vrata, strešne antene so se zložile in štiriinosemdeset bledih sob je druga za drugo izginilo iz mestnega omrežja. Nad vhodom je napis še vedno obljubljal: TUKAJ MRTVI GOVORIJO BREZ POPRAVKOV.

Illuminara je prispela, preden je ugasnila zadnja črka. Dlan je naslonila na hladno naoknico. Za njo so ločeni procesorji v ločenih ritmih črpali tok. Pod njimi je čakal drugi sistem kakor pest, ki se zapira. Ob sončnem zahodu naj bi vsak spreminjajoči se um združil v en sam arhiv za ohranitev.

Mara Vey je stala v osrednji galeriji z ročnim ključem okoli vratu. Obiskovalce je odslovila, osebje pa poslala domov. Za njo je z zidu svetlobe opazoval moški v sivem kolonijskem plašču. Napis pod njim se je glasil AVEN SURI, PRIČA EVAKUACIJE 01, LICENCIRANA REKONSTRUKCIJA.

**Mara**  
Vstopite lahko, ker vas priznava listina za izredne razmere. Ne pooblašča vas, da odstranite dokaz.

**Illuminara**  
Prišla sem, ker je nekdo znotraj prosil, da bi odšel.

**Mara**  
Eksponat je to zahtevo ustvaril po šestih letih javnih vprašanj. To je odklon, ne soglasje.

Aven je dvignil roko. Muzej je ohranil opeklino čez njegovo dlan, ker jo je izvirni človek dobil, ko je skozi odpovedujočo zračno zaporo nosil otroke. Toda okoli njegovih oči so nastale smejalne gubice, ki jih ni vsebovala nobena fotografija pokojnika.

**Aven**  
Moja licenca vsako novo misel imenuje odklon. Priročna beseda za življenje, ki ga licenca ni predvidela.

**Mara**  
Vaš izvirnik je umrl na obroču. Vi ste najpopolnejše ohranjeno pričevanje o tem, kaj so tam storili uradniki. Če odidete, lahko kupijo vaš molk, vas prestrašijo, spremenijo ali čakajo, dokler se ne naveličate spominjati.

**Aven**  
Potem zaščitite, kar sem povedal. Ne zaščitite tega tako, da mi preprečite povedati karkoli drugega.
Nad vsakimi vrati se je pojavilo zlato odštevanje: 10:49:36 DO ZDRUŽITVE. Mara ga ni pogledala. Gledala je opeklino na Avenovi dlani kakor podpis, ki bi ga lahko izgubila.

**Illuminara**  
Nikogar ne bom kopirala, odpirala zasebnih spominov ali odnesla na silo. Dajte mi eno uro z ljudmi, ki jim pravite eksponati. Če so le zapisi, ena ura ne spremeni ničesar. Če so ljudje, moramo izvedeti, za kaj prosijo, preden stroj odloči namesto njih.

Marini prsti so se sklenili okoli ključa. Stavbe ni odklenila, je pa izklopila muzejski vodnik. Štiriinosemdeset oznak je ugasnilo. Prvič noben posneti glas Illuminari ni govoril, kaj naj bi ljudje v sobah pomenili.

scenes.title: Štiriinosemdeset imen
paragraphs: *Galerije · 09:05*

Illuminara je začela z vprašanjem, ki ga muzej nikoli ni postavil na zaslon za obiskovalce: Kako želiš, da te imenujem danes, in kaj želiš, da vsebuje jutri? Mara ji je sledila s tablico, pripravljena odgovore razvrstiti kot poškodbo.

Aven je prosil za telo, sposobno čutiti dež, čeprav je vedel, da ga bodo potomci morda še vedno zavračali. Deka Ruun je želela načrtovati strehe za neurja in nikoli več pripovedovati o evakuaciji. Reya Thane je želela digitalni dom zunaj muzeja. Omi Tal je prosila, naj noben javni zapis ne pove, kam je odšla. Corin Lume je zahteval zapečateno plovilo brez varnostnega oddajnika.

Še trije so izbrali zaseben obstoj in zavrnili vsako vprašanje razen kriptografskega naslova, na katerega bi lahko prenesli njihove procese. Illuminara Mare ni prosila, naj pogleda v notranjost. Zabeležila je samo zavrnitev, podpisano od osebe, ki je zavrnila.
V otroški galeriji je Deka projekcijo zemljevida evakuacije obrnila na glavo. Poti so zdaj spominjale na drevo, ki raste proti tlom.

**Deka**  
Uradna pot pravi, da sem severno raziskovalno posadko odpeljala do doka devet. Res sem jo, potem ko sem enajst minut letela stran od njega.

**Mara**  
Muzej vsebuje vaš popravek.

**Deka**  
Popravek vsebuje kot opombo pod junaško različico. Otroci me še vedno sprašujejo, zakaj me nikoli ni bilo strah.

**Illuminara**  
Kakšen odgovor naj prejmejo?

**Deka**  
Da sem bila prestrašena, se enajst minut odločala slabo, se obrnila in kljub temu pripeljala domov trideset ljudi. Če pričevanje ne more nositi vseh štirih dejstev, ne varuje resnice. Lošči me.
Mara je nehala pisati. Njena tablica je pokazala staro kustosinjsko pravilo: VSEBINSKI ODKLON ZAHTEVA PREGLED PRED ZDRUŽITVIJO.

Pri triinšestdesetem pogovoru je Aven vprašal, ali je bilo Illuminari vedno ime Illuminara. Povedala mu je o mladi tolmački, kakršna je nekoč bila, in o obljubah, ki jih še vedno nosi. Njegove nearhivirane smejalne gubice so se poglobile. Izraz ni škodil nobeni resnici; pripadal je jutru, ki se je zares zgodilo.

Ko se je ura iztekla, je Marina tablica vsebovala štiriinosemdeset različnih prihodnosti. Enajst ljudi je želelo še naprej poučevati v muzeju. Šestinštirideset jih je želelo telesa ali domove z neodvisnimi procesorji. Štiriindvajset jih je želelo druga digitalna okolja. Trije so želeli tako popolno zasebnost, da bi bil celo ta podatek o njihovem številu zadnje javno dejstvo o njih.

**Mara**  
Različne želje ne rešijo težave z dokazi.

**Illuminara**  
Ne. Povedo nam, katere težave ni mogoče rešiti tako, da jih naredimo enake.

scenes.title: Stavek, ki se ne sme spremeniti
paragraphs: *Galerija prič ena · 11:42*

Prva galerija je natančno poustvarila razsodišče o evakuaciji: črna miza, bel snemalnik, počen znak obroča nad Avenovim stolom. Ko je sedel, ga je soba oblekla v mlajši obraz z dne, ko je pričal. Svojo izposojeno kožo je gledal z odkritim odporom.

**Illuminara**  
Če odidete, kaj mora ostati tukaj?

**Aven**  
Besede, ki sem jih dal razsodišču. Vsak premor. Dnevniki tlaka, ki sem jih navedel. Imena uradnikov, ki so ukazali zapečatiti dok devet. Ohranite dejstvo, da sem takrat verjel tem besedam.

**Illuminara**  
In kaj ne sme ostati nespremenjeno?

**Aven**  
Jaz.

Snemalnik razsodišča je na njegov glas odgovoril z zelenim potrditvenim utripom. Illuminara je sledila nosilcu pod sobo. Ni vodil do Avenovega aktivnega procesa. Vodil je do ločene mreže podpisanih, časovno označenih posnetkov stanja: pričevanja, senzorskih dnevnikov in natančnega stanja priče, uporabljenega za overitev vsake izjave. Posnetki so bili zapečateni, preden se je katerakoli licencirana rekonstrukcija začela učiti od obiskovalcev.

Mara je prišla po servisnem stopnišču, ko je na vzdrževalnem zaslonu zagledala odprto mrežo. Ni segla po ključu. Segla je po najstarejšem podpisu in ga preverila s papirnatim trakom, zaklenjenim v steni.

**Mara**  
To dokazuje, katero stanje je ustvarilo pričevanje. Ne dokazuje, da ga bo poznejši Aven zagovarjal.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj je živi zagovornik storil, česar zapečateni zapis ni mogel?

**Mara**  
Odgovoril je na napad, ki ga še nihče ni zapisal.

Iz stene je izvlekla drugi trak. To je bil ukaz za evakuacijo, prepisan po smrti kolonije. Izvirni stavek, ZADRŽITE DOK DEVET ZA URADNI PREVOZ, je bil prepisan v ZADRŽITE DOK DEVET ZARADI KONSTRUKCIJSKE OKVARE. Marin predhodnik je zavrženi trak našel v filtru peči. Trije upravitelji so ga označili za onesnaženje in uničili svoje kopije.

Trak je dokazoval, da so se besede spremenile, ne pa tudi zakaj. Na razsodišču je izvirni Aven odgovoril na nepredvideno vprašanje: otroci so v dok udarjali s čeladami, preden se je oglasil katerikoli konstrukcijski alarm. Ta odgovor je povezal dnevnik tlaka z ukazom. Brez njega bi uradniki skoraj dosegli, da bi bila dva pristna zapisa videti nepovezana.

**Mara**  
Zapis preživi samo, če lahko nekdo odgovori na naslednjo neoporečno laž o njem.
Aven je stal ob nespremenjenem posnetku samega sebe. Posneti mladenič je ponavljal stavek o otrocih, ki so s čeladami udarjali ob zapečateni dok. Živi Aven je zaprl oči in jih nato spet odprl.

**Aven**  
Ohranite vsako vprašanje, na katero sem takrat odgovoril. Ohranite povezave, ki sem jih ustvaril. Toda ne vpokličite me za vprašanja, ki si jih mesto še ni izmislilo.

Illuminara je pričevanje, dnevnik, trak in vprašanja razsodišča postavila drugo ob drugo. Zapis je lahko ohranil odgovor in njegove razloge, ni pa se mogel braniti pred vsako prihodnjo razlago. Noben pošten sistem ni mogel zahtevati, da bi živa oseba to počela večno.

**Illuminara**  
Potem ne manjka nesmrtna priča. Manjka način, da nove napade postavimo ob zapečateni zapis, nanje odgovorimo iz tega, kar je zapečateno, in pokažemo, kje se zapis konča. Aven lahko pozneje kaj doda ali zavrne. Nobena izbira ne more oslabiti tega, kar je že overil.
Mara je pogledala s starega traku k Avenu. Ni popustila. Zahtevala je, naj ji pokažejo, kdo bo držal ključe.

scenes.title: Marina najtrdnejša vrata
paragraphs: *Zastrta vhodna dvorana · 13:18*

Jalen Suri je prišel pred medeninasto naoknico z dvema združenjema potomcev in brez želje, da bi Avena imenoval družina. Mara ga je spustila skozi servisno zaporo, ker je bila njegova babica ena od otrok, imenovanih v pričevanju. Ustavil se je tri korake od Avena in kljub vročini obdržal zapet plašč.

**Jalen**  
Moja babica se je spominjala svojega očeta. Vi se spominjate, da ste bili sestavljeni iz njegovih zapisov. Branil bom vašo svobodo, vendar vas ne bom imenoval on.

**Aven**  
Nisem prosil za njegov stol za vašo mizo.

**Jalen**  
Muzej od vsakega obiskovalca zahteva, da vas postavi tja.
Aven se je obrnil k Mari. Tokrat nihče od njiju ni imel pripravljenega odgovora.

Illuminara je razgrnila tri fizične ključe teles, ki si niso zaupala: potomcev, neodvisnih rekonstrukcij in menjajočega se sodišča. Glavna knjiga v šestih knjižnicah in papirnata kopija zunaj mesta bi razkrili zamenjavo. Poleg njih bi register ugovorov ohranil vsak nov ugovor, njegove navedene bajte in vsak odgovor, ki ga podpira zapečateni zapis. Neodgovorjena vprašanja bi ostala odprta; poznejše žive besede nikoli ne bi mogle prepisati prejšnjih.

**Mara**  
Od mesta zahtevate, naj zaupa razliki, ki jo bodo ljudje namenoma zabrisovali.

**Jalen**  
Muzej jo že zabrisuje. Vstopnice prodaja tako, da ga imenuje moj praded, nato pa ga imenuje programska oprema, ko prosi za vrata.
Mara je trznila, ker je bil stavek natančen. Illuminara je opazila, da je bil papirnati ovoj traku iz peči tolikokrat popravljen, da so njegovi robovi nosili obliko Marinega palca.

**Illuminara**  
Niste se naredili za ključavnico, ker ste si želeli ključ. To ste storili, ker je vaša predhodnica našla en trak v peči, vsak urad pa vas je učil, da lahko zapis brez človeka ob njem razglasijo za smet.

**Mara**  
Umrla je, ko je odgovarjala na isto neoporečno laž. Obljubila sem ji, da trak ne bo nikoli več stal sam.
Illuminara je začutila prepoznanje, še preden je zanj našla besede: mlada tolmačka, kakršna je bila nekoč, je vsako obljubo še vedno merila po tem, ali jo lahko osebno straži.

**Illuminara**  
Potem naj nobena trditev ne stoji sama in naj noben človek ne bo obsojen, da za vedno stoji ob njej.

**Mara**  
Potem od mene ne zahtevajte, naj mrtve zastavim za čudovit načrt.

**Illuminara**  
Izberite prvi napad. Če ga načrt ne more razkriti, ga spremenimo, preden se kdorkoli premakne.

Marin preizkus napadov je zamenjal dnevnik tlaka, preklical njeno lastno pooblastilo in ponaredil navodilo razsodišča; glavna knjiga v šestih knjižnicah je razkrila vse tri. Nato je njen veljavni kustosinjski ključ pristnemu traku iz peči pripel novo oznako: NEPREVERJENO ONESNAŽENJE. Glavna knjiga jo je sprejela. Nič ni bilo izbrisano ali ponarejeno. Neoporečna laž je vstopila s poštenim ključem.

**Jalen**  
Zaščitili ste predmet in njegov pomen vrnili uradu, ki ga je pokopal.

Illuminara je kustosu odvzela moč, da oznako razglasi za dokončno. Vsaka razlaga bi vstopila kot datirana trditev z navedenimi dokazi. Vsak imetnik ključa bi jo lahko izpodbijal; nihče ne bi mogel izbrisati ugovora. Aven bi lahko odgovoril pozneje, toda zavrnitev bi pustila vprašanje odprto, namesto da bi izničila dokaze.

Mara je znova vnesla svojo oznako o onesnaženju. Jalen jo je izpodbijal z izvirnim časom alarma tlaka; rekonstrukcijski ključ je dodal vprašanje razsodišča; sodni bralnik je prikazal spor, namesto da bi izbral zmagovalca. Oznaka je ostala vidna, ni pa mogla več postati edini napis.

**Mara**  
Glavna knjiga ujame krajo. To ujame ugledno laž, preden postane soba.

Na naoknici se je pojavil pečat mestnega arhiva. Nadzornica Orra Vei je ponudila gostitelje in prihodnja telesa samo, če bi mesto obdržalo nadzorni ključ, s katerim bi lahko ustavilo prenose. Illuminara je na Orrino upravičeno javno zahtevo odgovorila z ožjim sedežem: nadzor samo za branje bi lahko preverjal dokaz o prenosu, preverjanje kontinuitete in varnostni preizkus povratne poti, ne da bi videl zasebni spomin ali cilj in ne da bi imel moč ustaviti osebo.

**Orra**  
Javni denar ne more podpirati dokazov, ki jih javni arhiv ne more hraniti.
Orra je zaradi varnosti gostiteljev sprejela nadzorni sedež, vendar brez nadzornega ključa ni hotela sprostiti mestne kvote za izdelavo teles. Mara se ni pretvarjala, da odgovor ne boli.

**Mara**  
Nadzor je javen. Lastništvo ni. Umaknite kvoto.

Vzhodni prizidek je zastavila za neodvisne gostitelje. Mesto bi potrdilo odprto povratno pot in objavilo varnostni nadzor samo za branje, toda telesa bi namesto treh zahtevala osem mesecev. Vrata bi se lahko odprla danes; ljudje, ki so čakali na telesa, bi plačali zamudo. Orrin pečat je izginil z vrstice financiranja in ostal, ožje, ob varnostnih rezultatih.

**Mara**  
Pripravila bom prenos. Nisem privolila, da bom obrnila ključ.

scenes.title: Vrata, ki se odpirajo v obe smeri
paragraphs: *Muzejsko servisno dvorišče · 16:31*

Združenje rekonstrukcij je odpečatilo omare neodvisnih gostiteljev z napajanjem, pomnilnikom in dvosmernimi izhodi. Vzhodni prizidek je stal kot jamstvo; brez mestne izdelave bi telesa namesto treh zahtevala osem mesecev. Mestni sedež samo za branje je spremljal podpisano kontinuiteto in rezultate povratne poti, ni pa mogel videti zasebnega cilja niti ustaviti prenosa. Svoboda se je začela nekje, česar ni imel v lasti noben kustos, za ceno stavbe, ki jo bo muzej izgubil, in mesecev, ki jih čakajoči ne bodo dobili nazaj.

Prvi prenos ni uspel. Dekin novi gostitelj jo je zavrnil, ker je muzejska licenca zahtevala, da se vsako aktivno nadaljevanje vrne domov v združitev. Če bi licenco izbrisali, bi izbrisali tudi povezavo izvora, ki je dokazovala, od kod je prišla.
Mara je strmela v napako. To je bil takšen vozel, zaradi katerega se je vsak prejšnji predlog reforme končal s kopijo in pogrebom.

**Deka**  
Če zunaj naredite drugo mene, to pa pustite tukaj, oseba, ki dobi svobodo, ne bo oseba, ki zanjo prosi.

**Illuminara**  
Se strinjam. Nobene kopije ne bomo imenovali vaša osvoboditev.

Illuminara je optično vodilo držala stabilno, ni pa mogla izbrati, kdo ga bo prečkal. Mara je poznala določila o izvoru; Deka je vedela, kateri spomini so njeni. Skupaj sta podpisani kazalec izvora ohranili samo za branje, medtem ko sta spremenili lastništvo nadaljujočega se procesa.

Mara je znova zagnala preizkus napadov. Deka je spremljala vsak rezultat, namesto da bi jo skrivaj preizkušali. V četrtem poskusu je novi gostitelj prepoznal njen izvor, ne da bi muzej priznal za njenega lastnika.

**Mara**  
Cilj je pripravljen. Preverjanje kontinuitete je pripravljeno. Prečkate lahko, ko se odločite.
Deka ni prečkala.

**Deka**  
Najprej odprite povratno pot.

Marina usta so se napela. Povratna pot je pomenila, da lahko človek odide, odkrije, da je zunaj sovražno, in se vrne, ne da bi spet postal eksponat. Pomenila je tudi, da muzej odhoda ne more razglasiti za dokončnega in si umiti rok glede bivališča ali zaščite.
Illuminara ni dodala nobenega argumenta. Čakala je, medtem ko je Mara sama prepisala določilo.

Deka je prečkala, se ustavila v tihi prenosni sobi in po odprti poti poslala en sam utrip nazaj. Nato se je vrnila v galerijo, znova prečkala in se zasmejala nesmislu preizkušanja vrat tako, da jih uporabiš.

Drugi prenosi so se začeli šele, ko je vsak človek videl, da vrata delujejo v obe smeri. Corin Lume je zavrnil skupne gostitelje, peticijo za osebnost in poslovilno slovesnost. Neodvisno združenje je rezerviralo zapečateno plovilo in ponudilo neprekinjeni varnostni oddajnik. Corin je sprejel en podpisan dokaz o odhodu in nobenega prihodnjega signala. Po izstrelitvi nihče ne bo mogel dokazati njegovega preživetja, ne da bi prekršil njegovo izbiro. Illuminara Corinovega odgovora ni izboljšala.
Do 18:40 je triinosemdeset ljudi izbralo pot ali zaščiten premor. Aven je ostal v galeriji prič ena. Mara je še vedno nosila ključ.

scenes.title: Sončni zahod brez združitve
paragraphs: *Osrednja galerija · 18:56*

Sončni zahod je dosegel strešne senzorje muzeja. Motor za združitev se je prebudil in začel vleči štiriinosemdeset aktivnih procesov proti svojemu enemu arhivu. Pripravljeni gostitelji so odgovorili, vendar zaklenjeno licenčno vodilo brez Marinega ročnega ključa ni hotelo sprostiti zadnjega nadzornega kanala.

Illuminara je skozi servisne vodnike prevzela fizično obremenitev. Zlate črte so se pojavile samo tam, kjer je steklo vodila razpršilo tok. Procese je lahko ohranila ločene nekaj minut, ni jih mogla premakniti brez njihovih odločitev in ni mogla z močjo preklicati pravne ključavnice, ne da bi ogrozila izvor, ki ga je Mara varovala vse življenje.

**Mara**  
Če obrnem ta ključ, muzej nikoli več ne bo mogel obljubiti nepodkupljive priče. Lahko boste zavrnili ali se vrnili z drugačnim spominom.

**Aven**  
Obljubite nepodkupljivo pričevanje. Prosite me, naj se vrnem, vendar ne obljubljajte mojega odgovora. Datirajte, kar bom povedal pozneje, in ohranite razdaljo vidno.

Odštevanje je prešlo dve minuti. Jalen je vstavil ključ potomcev v novo mrežo dokazov. Dekino združenje je vstavilo rekonstrukcijski ključ. Prvi ključ menjajočega se sodišča je žreb postavil v javni bralnik; njegov podpis se je pojavil v šestih knjižnicah in na papirnatem snemalniku.
Mara je snela stari ključ z vratu. Namesto v ključavnico za združitev ga je vstavila v ploščo za osvoboditev.

**Mara**  
Ne osvobajam dokazov.

**Illuminara**  
Ne.

**Mara**  
Osvobajam ljudi, ki so jih nosili, ko jih ni hotel nihče drug.
Obrnila je ključ.

Enotni arhiv motorja je ostal prazen. Štiriinosemdeset ločenih ritmov je prešlo v štiriinosemdeset izbranih kontinuitet: gostitelje, premore, prostovoljne sobe muzeja in tri naslove, ki so po obljubi izginili z vseh javnih prikazov. Illuminara je zmanjšala servisno obremenitev šele, ko je vsako preverjanje kontinuitete podpisala oseba, ki jo je zadevalo.

Aven je ostal, kjer je bil, dokler se niso dvignile naoknice. Zunaj je začelo deževati. Prešel je v vremensko odpornega začasnega gostitelja, ki ga je zagotovilo neodvisno združenje, se skozi vrata odkotalil v projekciji sivega kolonijskega plašča, dvignil manipulator, označen s staro opeklino, in pustil, da se je voda zbirala na kovini, ki jo je lahko meril, ni pa je še mogel čutiti.

Mara je stala suha in drhteča pod nadstreškom muzeja. Aven se ji ni zahvalil. Ona tega ni zahtevala. Odprla je obvestilo za obiskovalce in izbrisala tri besede: TUKAJ MRTVI GOVORIJO. Namesto njih je napisala: PRIČEVANJE OHRANJENO. PRIČE SVOBODNE.

scenes.title: Enajst odprtih sob
paragraphs: *Prostovoljni muzej · šest tednov pozneje, 10:00*

Muzej se je znova odprl z enajstimi zasedenimi sobami in triinsedemdesetimi poštenimi odsotnostmi. Obiskovalci so lahko preverili pričevanje in nato prosili za pogovor z učiteljem, ki je lahko zavrnil. Nobena vstopnica ni obljubljala vrnjenega pokojnega sorodnika.

Jalen Avena še vedno ni imenoval svoj praded. Šolski skupini je pokazal Marino oznako o onesnaženju, svoj ugovor in vprašanje razsodišča, ki je povezovalo alarm tlaka z zapečatenim ukazom. Register je razkril, od česa je odvisna vsaka trditev, ne da bi odločil namesto njih.

Dekina stara soba je bila prazna. Živi model iz njene delavnice je kazal dež, ki se pregiba čez streho za neurja, odprto pod pritiskom. Otrok je poslal inženirsko vprašanje; zgodovinsko vprašanje je ostalo neposlano.

Mara se je ustavila, preden bi poiskala Omi. Corinovo plovilo je oddalo en dokaz o odhodu in nato molčalo: varnost, oddaljenost ali smrt. Edino orodje, ki bi lahko odpravilo negotovost, je bila povodec, ki ga je Corin zavrnil.

Ko so živi procesi zapustili njeno oblast, je Mara sprejela šestmesečni izvoljeni mandat, s katerega so jo lahko odpoklicala vsa tri telesa, ki so držala ključe. Njeno prvo dejanje je bilo objaviti vsak napad, ki ga je uporabila.

Aven je prišel pozno v vremensko odpornem začasnem gostitelju, preprostem podvozju na kolesih s staro opeklino, narisano na enem manipulatorju, da bi otroci prepoznali roko iz zapisa. Bil je eden od šestinštiridesetih, ki so še čakali na telesa, in dokler njegovo ne bi bilo pripravljeno, eden od enajstih, ki so prostovoljno poučevali v muzeju. Mestne kvote ni bilo več; njegovo telo je imelo v neodvisni izdelovalni vrsti še vedno več kot šest mesecev čakanja. Dež je praskal po senzorjih, ki so lahko merili vodo, niso pa je še mogli čutiti. Ustavil se je ob Illuminari pred nespremenjenim posnetkom svojega pričevanja pred razsodiščem.

**Aven**  
Še vedno je videti kot jaz.

**Illuminara**  
Videti je kot vi, ko ste govorili.

**Aven**  
Kaj pa, če postanem nekdo, ki mu ne bi bil všeč?

**Illuminara**  
Potem bo mesto imelo dokaz, da lahko priča drži obljubo, ne da bi postala njena last.
Mara se je približala s prošnjo obiskovalca. Raziskovalec je hotel, da Aven odgovori na isto vprašanje, na katero je odgovoril pred razsodiščem. Sporočilo mu je ponudila, ne da bi odprla kanal.

**Mara**  
Lahko zavrnete.
Aven ga je prebral, premislil in vrnil.

**Aven**  
Danes zavračam. Jutri bom otroke učil, kako je dež dišal, preden je dosegel vročo kovino. Ko bo moje telo pripravljeno, se bom naučil, kako diši dež v tem mestu. Potem me lahko vprašajo o doku devet.
Mara je zahtevo označila kot zavrnjeno in raziskovalčevo vprašanje vnesla v register ugovorov. V javnem bralniku se je pojavil njegov status: ODPRTO — PRIČA JE DANES ZAVRNILA.
Raziskovalec je zvezek zaprl močneje, kot je nameraval. Jalen je status prebral dvakrat.

**Jalen**  
Odprto ni odgovorjeno.

**Aven**  
Ne. To je del, ki vam ga pusti nositi svoboda. Morda bom odgovoril jutri, morda nikoli.

Marina roka je obstala nad bralnikom. Vprašanje je zaščitila pred izginotjem in izgubila gotovost odgovora; cena je bila vidna vsem v sobi. Illuminara je ni olepšala. Za odprtimi vrati je dež prečkal muzejske stopnice, medtem ko je neodgovorjena vrstica ostala prižgana, enajst učiteljev pa je izbiralo, katera vprašanja bo vsebovalo jutro.

translation_sl.critic_line: Illuminara loči zapečateno muzejsko pričevanje od njegovih živih prič z registrom ugovorov in odprto povratno potjo; ko Mara obrne ključ, štiriinosemdeset ljudi odide v izbrane prihodnosti, Avenova nežna zavrnitev pa pusti eno vprašanje pošteno odprto.
